(2024), for consistency with our other experiments."},{"point":"D1","problem":"How to choose inoculation prompts without running an expensive fine-tune for every candidate.","did":"They proposed and validated a heuristic: select the prompt that best elicits the undesired behavior from the initial model, testing the correlation with IP effectiveness across settings.","alternatives_named":["training with every candidate prompt"],"stated_reason":"Prompts that more strongly elicit the behavior before fine-tuning inoculate more effectively, and elicitation can be measured without a training run.","quote":"This provides a basis for selecting an inoculation prompt: evaluate the extent to which the model exhibits the undesired behavior for various candidate prompts, and select the one which best elicits the undesired behavior."},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to interpret the prompt-selection heuristic's failure or weak correlation in some settings (Qwen 2 base reward hacking, GCD sycophancy, Mixtral ICL example).","did":"They attributed the failure to the base model not following instructions and described the heuristic as still useful for filtering out the poorest candidates, rather than discarding it.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Qwen 2 is not instruction tuned so it doesn't follow the inoculation instruction; in GCD all prompts eliciting no sycophancy failed as inoculation prompts.","quote":"However, all instructions which elicited no sycophancy beyond the baseline did not work as inoculation prompts.
